# Original .NET CLI fixtures

Compiler-generated C# sugar/state-machine inputs are separately documented in
[`sugar/README.md`](sugar/README.md). Their committed DLL and independent PEReader
expectations need no .NET for ordinary tests; only explicit regeneration uses the
pinned SDK. The handcrafted fixtures below retain their existing toolchain.

`Fixture.dll` is a deterministic, handcrafted PE32/ECMA-335 managed module.
It is original repository test data, generated by `generate.py` with Python 3
standard library only. It includes no copied assemblies, proprietary compiler
output or third-party runtime code. No C# compiler or .NET installation is
required to regenerate it; no analyzed method is executed by the tests.

Run `python3 tests/fixtures/dotnet/generate.py` from the repository root.
`expected.json` records the independently specified method tokens and original
IL bytes, input size and SHA-256. These expectations come from the handcrafted
assembler inputs, not from rxd output. The PE timestamp and MVID are fixed.

The fixture contains arithmetic, checked overflow, unsigned comparison,
managed-reference loads, volatile prefix, field writes, discarded and duplicated
call results, a non-empty branch stack merge, one finally handler and a Unicode
user string/type namespace, plus an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate retained as code units. `Effect` increments a static field, so dropping or
duplicating its evaluation changes behavior even when its return value is unused.
The fixture is intended for static analysis and has no process entry point.

The test suite derives truncated and modified copies in temporary directories
for malformed-input and content-identity checks. It retains the original
method IL even when reconstruction is unsupported.

Additional probes cover nested finally continuations (return storage must observe
the inner and then outer write), distinct normal-leave/fault behavior, catch entry
objects, filter side effects, nested rethrow, and forbidden branches bypassing
cleanup. Value-type probes cover copies, managed addresses, constructors, instance
calls, object/array operations and prefix attachment; GenericIdentity preserves an
open method type parameter. GenericCaller, GenericOwnerField and GenericMixedCaller
keep caller method parameters distinct from the referenced type/method parameters;
GenericExternalCall deliberately omits required method instantiation. AliasClassValue
derives from a local class named System.Enum in a non-core assembly and must keep
an object receiver; the spelling alone cannot identify a CLR enum. VolatileAdd deliberately has an invalid prefix target.
The original twelve MethodDef tokens remain fixed; hashes bind the expanded bytes.

These independently assembled probes exercise semantic cases also represented in
ILSpy's pinned tests: `Correctness/StackTypes.il`, `Correctness/StackTests.il`, and
`Pretty/ExceptionHandling.cs`. The implementation is cross-referenced against
`IL/ILReader.cs` (handler entry stacks and prefixes) and `IL/BlockBuilder.cs`
(region nesting), at commit `3491b15e6b99b6cbaf1f1495184d48d8a32d554c`.
No ILSpy source or tests are copied into these fixture bytes. Cross-reference does
not make ILSpy's default expression simplification a strict equivalence oracle.

`python3 tests/fixtures/dotnet/generate.py --invalid-reference` regenerates
`InvalidReference.dll`: two attributes share a constructor token, and the second
attribute has an out-of-range MethodDef parent. Its rejection verifies that
successful token-check caching does not suppress a later invalid relationship.
`invalid-reference.json` independently records its source hash and layout.
